evidence: Cic. Off. 1.13 fin.: fraus quasi vulpēculae, vīs leōnis vidētur (Lewis & Short)

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation; aliquem aliquā rē
evidence: Cic. Att. 1.1.3: cum Caecilius ā Variō magnā pecūniā fraudārētur (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fl. 48: fraudātōrum et īnfitiātōrum impudentia (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: an impostor, a con man, a swindler
evidence: Cic. Clu. 72: ille plānus improbissimus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short prints plănus with a short a (Greek πλάνος), unlike the adjective plānus, flat.

phrases.english: to convict someone on many counts of fraud

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 194–195, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
